01 / FOUNDATIONS

Color roles

Semantic aliases → foundation values

Format, Audience, and Voice keep their distinct backgrounds. Blue identifies the primary action and selection border.

Typography

Inter + Newsreader

Interface text uses Inter. Newsreader is used for the home greeting, project-start heading, and serif-formatted articles. Composite type tokens export one CSS variable per property.

Space & shape

4 px rhythm · 2 px refinements
4Status / checkbox / detail
8Field / menu / toolbar / panel / card
16Button / dialog / popover / project card
999Pill / circle

Four radius primitives: 4, 8, 16, and 999 px. Component aliases map each interface element to this shared scale.

Surfaces

Subtle menu elevation
Dropdown
Popover
Dialog

Open dropdowns and floating menus use a 0px 4px 12px neutral shadow: 8% opacity on desktop and 16% on mobile. Mobile dialogs and open workspace panels share New Project’s 16% backdrop and 2px blur. Other surfaces remain flat; keyboard-focus outlines remain visible.

Iconography

CSA icon library

Unselected: outlined (FILL 0). Selected: filled (FILL 1). Apply this rule to icons in selection controls, including view switches, source folders, and formatting toggles. Actions without a selected state use filled icons.

All Material Symbols icons currently used in the app are shown below. Each icon shows both states and its Material Symbols name. Default glyph size is 24 px; Draft is 14 px.

02 / COMPONENTS

The pieces of the workspace.

These specimens use the production component stylesheet. Try a state to see how it responds.

Primary uses white text on Blue 600, Blue 700 on hover, and Blue 200 when disabled. Secondary keeps a white surface with Blue 600 text and outline, Blue 700 on hover, and Blue 200 when disabled. Tertiary uses Blue 600 text without a resting border; hover adds a Blue 700 outline and label on white. Disabled tertiary labels use Blue 200. The middle column previews hover. Keyboard focus keeps the visible shared ring.

Text contrast: Blue 600 and white measure 5.17:1; Blue 700 and white measure 6.70:1. Blue 600 text on the page canvas measures 5.02:1. All enabled and hover combinations meet the 4.5:1 normal-text AA target. Disabled states are exempt from contrast minimums.

Destructive and icon actions

Semantic variants and utility controls

Cancel uses the standard secondary button: white fill, Blue 600 outline and label. Delete uses Red 700 with a white label, and Red 800 on hover or press. Both use 46 px height, 16 px radius, and 16 px semibold labels. Disabled Delete uses a neutral surface. Icon actions retain their utility styling and accessible names.

Status labels use the shared detail corners (4 px). Settings chips use pill corners. Pair status color with its label and icon.

Selection fields

14 px / 600 · 36 px desktop · 46 px mobile

Format, Audience, and Voice each display their single fixed setting using the app’s shared fields and chip colors.

Toast notifications

Compact feedback with an optional Undo action
deleteSource deleted

Deletion feedback uses the shared white toast, a blue trash icon in a pale blue circle, and an outlined Undo button. Undo restores the message and removes the action. Other notifications use the same white surface without a deletion icon.

Send to WordPress

Destination dialog

The dialog uses the app’s heading, destination listbox, Cancel, and Send controls. Each option shows a destination name and URL. The four publisher destinations also show a noninteractive ADMIN VIEW badge. The selected row and hover use light gray; the panel uses a white surface, border, shadow, and 8 px corners. This specimen changes only the reference.

Adaptation status segments

Inter 14 / 400 · 36 px desktop · 46 px mobile

The selected segment uses the secondary button’s white background, blue text, and blue border; hover uses its shared secondary colors. Inactive segments use the same dark text with or without a count. Empty sections read To Adapt or Adapted. Pending counts read 1 Content to Adapt or 2 Content to Adapt; completed counts read 4 Adapted. The Adapt action belongs to To Adapt.

Content card

Standard FormatGeneral AudienceUS Weekly235 Words

Adapted cards use a solid border; the selected card uses Blue 600. Pending cards keep the dashed SVG border and selection checkbox. Settings and the outlined actual word-count pill stay on one line with a fade when more labels are offscreen; scroll the row to see them. Content cards do not show a source counter. Each card has a compact 16 px pencil at the top right. It opens an anchored menu with a red trash icon and Delete label for either pending or adapted content. The menu uses the dashboard menu’s white surface, border, shadow, and rounded corners. Escape or clicking outside closes it; Escape returns focus to the pencil. This sample changes only this page.

Editor metadata

Tab status and header details

Editor tabs show the draft status and title. The editor header shows Format, Audience, Voice, and a borderless source counter after the settings, with no word-count pill. The source counter keeps dark text and icon. Its background stays transparent at rest and while expanded; only hover adds a light-gray pill using the shared 24 px chip height. The source action retains a 44 px click target. Actual draft word counts remain on content cards and in the editor footer.

Editor toolbar

8 px radius · 2 px vertical padding

A Neighborhood Project Brings a Community Together

Rounded border encloses the controls and dividers. Use foundation.space.20 (20 px) between the title, toolbar, and body. On small screens, scroll within the toolbar to reach every action. Controls: Bold, Italic, Underline, H2, H3, block quote, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Undo, and Redo. This specimen previews formatting states.

04 / HANDOFF

Ready to use and maintain.

The app now reads its shared values from the same token source as this reference.

Use the system

  1. Edit dist/design-system/tokens.json.
  2. Run npm run design-system:build.
  3. Use a semantic or component CSS variable.
  4. Run npm run check and review desktop and mobile.
.primary-action {
  background: var(--csa-component-button-primary-background);
  color: var(--csa-component-button-primary-label);
  height: var(--csa-component-button-height);
  border-radius: var(--csa-component-button-radius);
}

Keep generated CSS, flat JSON, and CSV in sync. The check command detects stale exports, unresolved references, cycles, and CSS naming collisions.

Design-tool handoff

Use DTCG-compatible JSON in a token importer that supports the 2025.10 format. CSV includes slash-separated design names, resolved values, aliases, and descriptions for manual mapping.

Map colors and dimensions to variables where supported. Map typography to text styles. Check alias and composite support in your importer.

Source: CSA b92005e. This extraction preserves the existing light theme; no additional theme or invented color ramp is included.

Responsive behavior

≤ 768 px
Mobile navigation, stacked canvas, 46 px selection fields, 44 px touch targets.
≥ 769 px
Desktop navigation and workspace panels.
≤ 1100 px
Editor layout adapts before the mobile navigation breakpoint.
999 / 579 px
Dashboard container widths switch to two and one columns.

Additional component-specific breakpoints: 700, 650, 480, and 370 px. CSS media and container queries retain literal values because custom properties cannot replace query thresholds.

Motion & review notes

Most interactions run 120–200 ms. Arrival uses the observed 520 ms timing and cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). The app honors reduced-motion preferences.

The current palette is retained. Muted text on white is 2.52:1; white on primary blue is 5.17:1. Enabled button text meets the 4.5:1 AA target; muted text still needs review when used for active content.

The radius scale is standardized. Other observed values and component exceptions remain documented in the inventory.
